components.text: Specify how whole paradigms are compared when explanatory virtues and ontological or theoretical costs conflict.
Specify the method by which the Orthodox account is compared with alternative explanations and their costs.
Show that Orthodox belief or presupposition is necessary for coherent thought rather than merely for the speaker's preferred ultimate explanation.
Explain how paradigm-level circularity yields the specifically Orthodox necessity conclusion.
Show the connection between Orthodox presupposition and coherent thought despite nonbelievers' evident reasoning.
Explain why paradigm-level circularity establishes the particular necessity claim rather than merely describing worldview dependence.
Explain why assuming providential governance nontrivially justifies regularity rather than merely relocating the assumption induction requires.
Explain why assuming providential governance provides more justification than directly assuming natural regularities.
Identify the non-question-begging epistemic advantage providence has over directly assuming natural regularity.
Determine whether the objection addresses induction's meta-level epistemic justification rather than individual experimental success.
Establish that denial of non-contradiction becomes incoherent rather than merely producing a contradiction acceptable to a dialetheist.
Show why transcendental or paradigm-level circularity defeats a contradiction-tolerant opponent.
Show why paradigm-level reductio can reject a position whose adherent does not accept contradiction as defeating.
Explain why accepting a true contradiction supplies a reason the dialetheist accepts for rejecting the relevant assumption.
Explain why the reductio remains forceful when an opponent does not accept contradiction as automatically defeating.
Show that making one meaningful non-contradictory assertion commits the speaker to universal non-contradiction.
Show that making one meaningful non-contradictory assertion entails universal acceptance of non-contradiction.
Show that the logical regularities presupposed by meaningful grammar entail universal non-contradiction rather than merely local structure.
Address whether paradoxical or inconsistent discourse still relies on logical regularities in grammar and predication.
Show that rational access to abstract objects and moral truths uniquely requires Orthodox theism.
Distinguish dependence on logical structure from dependence on an Orthodox divine ground.
Challenge the claim that abstract and moral knowledge uniquely requires the Orthodox Christian God.
Explain how a non-theistic Platonist connects invariant abstract forms to changing particulars and human cognition.
Explain how a Platonist rational-access alternative connects invariant forms with changing minds and particulars.
Explain how locating abstract objects in God's mind preserves shared thought content without recreating a distinction between thinking and what is thought.
Show that locating abstract objects in God's mind explains shared content without recreating a thought-content distinction.
Explain shared abstract content while distinguishing created thoughts and essences from divine thoughts and God's essence.
Explain shared abstract content without identifying created thoughts or abstracta with God's mental act or essence.
Clarify whether alternative logical structures defeat the claim about logical norms operative in ordinary human experience.
Address whether the asserted necessities concern all possible systems or the structures instantiated in known experience.
Clarify whether the affirmative claim concerns necessary abstract structure or the paradigmatic structures of actual experience.
Show why structures dominant in ordinary experience establish necessary classical logical preconditions despite developed non-classical alternatives.
Distinguish indispensable linguistic regularity from the full necessity of classical logical principles.
Determine whether actual experiential entrenchment establishes necessary classical structure despite developed non-classical alternatives.
Determine what known experiential structures establish once alternative abstract systems are conceded.
Clarify whether alternative formal systems displace the structures actually used throughout ordinary known experience.
